name: AfterSell
summary: Post-purchase upsell and cross-sell app for Shopify (by Rokt): one-click upsells, downsells and thank-you-page offers plus checkout customization to lift average order value, with no extra ad spend.
best_for: Shopify stores with steady order volume that want to lift average order value with one-click post-purchase and checkout upsells
skip_if: your store gets only a trickle of orders: fix traffic and conversion first; there's nothing to upsell against low volume
honest_knock: Post-purchase upsells only move the needle with steady order volume and a sensible complementary-offer strategy: bolt it onto a store with little traffic and there's nothing to upsell. The no-rev-share model is a genuine plus over percentage-based rivals.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/aftersell and in our own test that day) Three plans, each metered by monthly order volume, read on aftersell.com/pricing and on the Shopify App Store listing on 22 September 2026 (re-verified 22 September 2026 and again 27 September 2026). The entry prices: Post-Purchase $34.99 a month for 200 monthly orders, capped at $999.99; Pre-Purchase $59.99 for 200, capped at $599.99; Complete $79.99, capped at $1,359.99 - and on 27 September 2026 the Complete card quotes that $79.99 for 500 monthly orders, where on 22 September it read 200 like the other two. The page does not say whether the Complete entry tier was widened or the card is wrong, so confirm the tier for your own volume in the app before you install. Complete is the other two together, which the vendor prices at 15% under buying them separately. Go over a volume tier and the fee steps up to the matching one on its own, with that cap as the ceiling. Every plan carries a 30-day free trial, all charges are billed in USD, and the Free plan on the listing is for development and partner stores only. Checkout upsells are Shopify Plus only and now sit inside Post-Purchase and Complete rather than being billed separately. Rokt Thanks, the third-party offers on the confirmation page, is free with no minimum order volume and pays up to $0.80 per order; for stores above 1,000 monthly orders whose primary market is the US, Canada, Australia or the UK those earnings are credited against the subscription dollar for dollar. Aftersell Max, for high-volume stores, is custom-priced and publishes no figure. The unexplained $19.99 we saw above the $79.99 on the Complete card on 22 September 2026 is no longer on the page on 27 September. This replaces the single order-volume ladder we recorded on 5 September 2026 ($34.99 for 0-500 orders, $54.99 for 501-1,000, $99.99 for 1,001-2,000); that ladder is on neither page any more. Read again on 17 November 2026: the listing (Aftersell Post Purchase Upsell, 4.9 from 1,130 reviews) still shows the Free card reading “ONLY For Development & Partner Stores” and the three entry prices, Post-Purchase $34.99, Pre-Purchase $59.99 and Complete $79.99 a month, each with a 30 day free trial, and no longer says anything about order volume. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store the app did not show the Free card. Its plan cards read Post-Purchase $34.99 a month with 5 cents per order above 500 orders, capped at $999.99; Pre-Purchase $59.99 with 3 cents per order above 500, capped at $599.99; and Complete $79.99 with 7 cents per order above 500, capped at $1,359.99, with a counter showing 2 monthly orders. That is a different description from the 200 order entry tiers and volume steps we took from the vendor's pricing page in September, so confirm in the app how your own volume is charged. Choosing Post-Purchase opened Shopify's approval screen: a 30 day free trial ending 17 December, an app spending limit of $999.99 per 30 days, the line “You will not be billed for this test charge” and an Add payment method row, so we did not approve it.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session installed AfterSell on a Shopify development store. Every page in the app showed only paid plan cards and no free development store plan; the Shopify approval screen for Post-purchase said there would be no charge for this test but also showed an Add payment method row, so it was not approved and no funnel was built. The app was uninstalled; nothing was paid. Install: the install started at about 23:23; the dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. After Install the app opened at about 23:24 on a plan screen. Core action NOT DONE: the app opens no funnel editor. Every page, also Post-purchase funnels in the app menu, shows only More revenue, less effort. with the plan cards. No funnel was built or previewed and the checkout settings of the store were not changed. Plans in the app: Post-purchase $34.99 a month, 5 cents per order above 500, caps at $999.99; Pre-purchase $59.99 a month, 3 cents per order above 500, caps at $599.99; Complete $79.99 a month, 7 cents per order above 500, caps at $1,359.99 (most popular); Max Custom. A counter showed 2 monthly orders, and checkout upsells are for Shopify Plus only. The free development store plan from the listing was not on the page. Checkout: Choose plan on Post-purchase opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the line You will not be billed for this test charge, a 30-day free trial ending on 17 Dec, plan AfterSell Pricing, an app spending limit of at most $999,99 USD per 30 days and a row Add payment method. Our rule is to approve nothing on a screen with an Add payment method row, so nothing was approved and no card was entered. Cancelling: no subscription existed. The app was removed in Settings, Apps, Uninstall; the dialog warns that data managed by the app will be deleted and needs a reason (Testing multiple apps). Clean up: the app is gone from Installed; no theme or checkout change and no order. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Every page of the app shows the plan cards until a plan is approved; the listing names a free development store plan that the app did not show; the approval screen said there would be no charge for this test but still showed an Add payment method row.
